lessons.title: 谓语的定义与限定核心
lessons.meta: 一个分句先找带时态或情态的谓语核心

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: works 是本分句唯一带现在时、并随 Mia 使用三单形式的动词，所以它是限定谓语。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: wants 带现在时，是限定谓语；to leave 没有时态，只整体填入 wants 后的宾语位置。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: 外层先看 I know，know 是主句限定谓语；that 从句内部另有 she agrees，不能把 agrees 算进主句谓语。

rules: 限定谓语体现时态或情态，并与主语建立句法关系。
非谓语形式不能单独构成独立分句的限定谓语。
复合句的每个分句各有自己的限定谓语，不能把从句谓语并入主句谓语。

questions.question: 哪个词是限定谓语？
questions.correct: works 带一般现在时并与 Mia 一致。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：works 带一般现在时并与 Mia 一致。

questions.question: 本句限定谓语是什么？
questions.correct: to leave 不带时态，限定谓语是 wants。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：to leave 不带时态，限定谓语是 wants。

questions.question: 主句谓语是什么？
questions.correct: agrees 属于 that 从句，外层谓语是 know。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：agrees 属于 that 从句，外层谓语是 know。

narration.text:
一句话里出现几个动词，不等于就有几个谓语。先找哪一个动词在负责整句话的时间、语气和主语变化，它像开关一样让一个小句真正成立。这个核心叫限定谓语。<#0.8#>
Mia works here。<#0.8#>Mia 是主语，works 一边说“工作”，一边把事情放在一般现在时，还和单数主语 Mia 对应。here 只补充工作地点，不属于谓语核心。<#0.8#>
Mia wants to leave。<#0.8#>这里有 wants 和 leave 两个动作意思，但只有 wants 在承担主句的时间和主语变化。to leave 只补充“想做什么”，自己不让主句成立，所以它是非谓语部分。看到两个动词形式，不能直接画成两个谓语。<#0.8#>
I know that she agrees。<#0.8#>先看外层，I 的限定谓语是 know。that 后面又有一套“谁怎么样”：she 是从句主语，agrees 是从句自己的限定谓语。这里确实有两个限定谓语，因为句中包含两个小句。<#0.8#>
判断时先划分小句；再在每个小句里找负责时间、语气或主语变化的动词；如果它后面还跟着其他动词形式，再把相关部分合成完整谓语。先分层，再数谓语，最不容易错。

lessons.title: 助动词链的顺序
lessons.meta: 情态、完成、进行、被动按固定槽位排列
examples: The bridge may have been repaired.

analyses.label: 进行助动词的过去分词

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: may 承担限定性和情态，begin 用原形；may begin 合起来才是完整谓语。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: may 是限定情态词，have 建立完成，been waiting 建立进行；四个词按“情态—完成—进行—实义动词”组成一个完整谓语。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: may 表可能，have 表完成，been repaired 表被动；它们不是三个谓语，而是一条“情态—完成—被动”助动词链。

rules: 情态动词位于助动词链最前，后接动词原形。
完成体 have 位于情态之后、进行或被动 be 之前。
完整链条遵循“情态＋have done＋be doing＋be done＋实义动词”的槽位顺序，实际只使用所需槽位。

questions.question: may 后应使用什么？
questions.correct: 情态动词后接原形 begin。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：情态动词后接原形 begin。

questions.question: 哪一个顺序正确？
questions.correct: 顺序是情态＋完成＋进行＋实义动词。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：顺序是情态＋完成＋进行＋实义动词。

questions.question: may have been repaired 同时表达什么？
questions.correct: may 表情态，have been 表完成被动链。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：may 表情态，have been 表完成被动链。

narration.text:
把一串助动词想成排队上车：谁站前面、谁站后面都有固定位置，不能随意换座。先抓住情态、完成、进行和被动这四层，长谓语就不会乱。<#0.9#>
先看，The work may begin soon.<#0.7#>may 先把整件事标成“可能”，begin 保持原形，两个词合起来才说完整。<#0.8#>
再看，She may have been waiting.<#0.7#>这次链条比第一句多了完成和进行：先是 may，再是 have，最后落到 been waiting。<#0.8#>
最后看，The bridge may have been repaired.<#0.7#>第三句没有进行这一层，may、have 和 been repaired 分别交代可能、较早完成和被动。<#0.9#>
遇到长谓语，从最左边开始读：先判断情态，再看完成、进行或被动，最后落到实义动作。缺哪层就跳过哪层，但顺序不能倒。

lessons.title: 谓语操作词
lessons.meta: 疑问、否定和倒装操作最前面的助动词

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: 陈述句中的第一个助动词 has 移到主语 she 前，承担疑问操作；has finished 仍共同表达完成体。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: has 是助动词链中第一个词，因此 not 紧跟 has；has not finished 合起来是否定的完整谓语。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: 陈述 Mia likes tea → 疑问 Does Mia like tea?

rules: 已有助动词时，第一个助动词承担倒装并移到主语前。
已有助动词时，not 放在第一个助动词之后。
一般时实义动词没有助动词时，用 do/does/did 提供操作词，实义动词恢复原形。

questions.question: She has finished 的一般疑问句怎样开头？
questions.correct: 已有 has，直接把第一个助动词前移。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：已有 has，直接把第一个助动词前移。

questions.question: not 应放在哪里？
questions.correct: 第一助动词 has 是否定操作词。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：第一助动词 has 是否定操作词。

questions.question: 哪句正确？
questions.correct: 三单标记由 Does 承担，like 用原形。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：三单标记由 Does 承担，like 用原形。

narration.text:
一句话要变成疑问或否定，通常不是整条谓语一起搬家，而是让最前面的助动词当“操作开关”。先找到这个开关，后面的变化会简单很多。<#0.9#>
先看，Has she finished?<#0.7#>原陈述句已经有 has，所以直接把它移到 she 前面，不需要另找帮手。<#0.8#>
再看，She has not finished.<#0.7#>变否定时 has 不搬家，not 紧跟在它后面，finished 继续保留过去分词。<#0.8#>
最后看，Does Mia like tea?<#0.7#>likes 原来独自承担三单；变疑问后这份变化交给 Does，like 就回到原形。<#0.9#>
做变句题时先问：原句有没有现成助动词？有，就操作第一个；没有，再请 do、does 或 did 来帮忙，并让实义动词回到原形。这样疑问、否定和时态都会落在同一个开关上。

lessons.title: 基础主谓一致
lessons.meta: 限定谓语与主语的人称和数一致

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: 主语中心 boy 是第三人称单数，限定谓语 plays 用 -s 与它一致。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: 主语 I 在现在时与 be 对应为 am；ready 是描述 I 的表语，不参与一致。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: Tom 和 Mia 是两个独立的人，and 把它们组成复数主语，因此限定系动词用 are。

rules: 一般现在时中，第三人称单数主语使用相应单数谓语。
be 的形式直接随主语人称、数和时间变化。
and 连接两个独立主语通常构成复数主语。

questions.question: The boy ___ football.
questions.correct: 中心主语 boy 是第三人称单数。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：中心主语 boy 是第三人称单数。

questions.question: I ___ ready.
questions.correct: 第一人称单数现在时用 am。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：第一人称单数现在时用 am。

questions.question: Tom and Mia ___ ready.
questions.correct: 两个独立主语并列，谓语用复数。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：两个独立主语并列，谓语用复数。

narration.text:
主谓一致可以先理解成“主语和限定动词要对上号”。现在时里，主语是一个人、两个人，或者是 I，动词给出的形式会不同。<#0.9#>
先看，The boy plays football.<#0.7#>boy 只表示一个第三人称对象，所以现在时的 play 要带上 s。<#0.8#>
再看，I am ready.<#0.7#>主语换成 I，be 就使用 am；ready 只是说明状态，不参与选择。<#0.8#>
最后看，Tom and Mia are ready.<#0.7#>Tom 和 Mia 被 and 连成两个人，主语按复数理解，因此使用 are。<#0.9#>
先圈完整主语，再判断它的人称和单复数，最后只检查限定谓语。表语、宾语和地点说明都不决定这次变化。简单句先把“谁”和“怎么样”对好，不要看见一个名词就去改动词。先确定主语范围，再动谓语。

lessons.title: 复杂主语找中心词
lessons.meta: 后置修饰语不改变主语中心词的数
examples: The box of books is heavy.
Mia, together with her friends, is here.
She is one of the students who work hard.

analyses.text: She is one of the students
analyses.label: 主句

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: 完整主语是 The box of books，中心词是单数 box；of books 只是后置修饰语，所以用 is。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: together with her friends 是附加说明，没有像 and 那样增加主语核心；限定谓语仍与 Mia 一致，用 is。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: 外层主干是 She is one of the students；who 在定语从句中指复数 students，所以从句限定谓语用 work。

rules: of、with 等介词短语修饰主语时，谓语与短语前的中心词一致。
together with、as well as、along with 引入附加成分，不构成 and 式复数主语。
关系从句中的谓语与关系词所指的先行词一致。

questions.question: The box of books ___ heavy.
questions.correct: 中心词 box 是单数。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：中心词 box 是单数。

questions.question: Mia, together with her friends, ___ here.
questions.correct: 主语中心仍是 Mia。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：主语中心仍是 Mia。

questions.question: who ___ hard 中谓语为何用 work？
questions.correct: 关系词在从句内指向 students。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：关系词在从句内指向 students。

narration.text:
主语一长，最容易被离动词最近的复数词带跑。正确做法像拆快递：先去掉外面的补充说明，找到真正决定单复数的中心词。<#0.9#>
先看，The box of books is heavy.<#0.7#>books 虽然靠近 is，却只是放在 of 后修饰 box；真正管单复数的是 box。<#0.8#>
再看，Mia, together with her friends, is here.<#0.7#>friends 也只是附加说明，核心主语仍是 Mia，所以不能被复数词带成 are。<#0.8#>
最后看，She is one of the students who work hard.<#0.7#>这一句要进入 who 从句判断：who 指回 students，从句里的 work 因此按复数处理。<#0.9#>
看到 of、with、together with 或关系从句时，先划清它们属于哪一层。限定谓语跟真正的主语中心一致，不是机械跟最近的名词一致。

lessons.title: 时态与体的时间关系
lessons.meta: 时态定位观察点，体展示事件内部状态

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: lives 的一般现在时把观察点放在现在，说明居住状态当前成立；now 只是帮助确认语境。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: is 承担现在时，reading 展示正在展开的过程；is reading 合起来是一个现在进行体谓语。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: have 承担现在时，read 表示先前完成；have read 把读书这件事与现在的结果或经验连接起来。

rules: 时态首先把观察点定位在现在或过去；时间词只是线索，语境关系才是依据。
体不等于时间：进行体显示过程，完成体显示“先发生并与观察点相关”。
同一事件可因说话者选择的观察方式不同而使用不同体。

questions.question: lives 主要把观察点放在哪里？
questions.correct: 一般现在时以现在为观察点。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：一般现在时以现在为观察点。

questions.question: 进行体突出什么？
questions.correct: is reading 把动作呈现为正在展开。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：is reading 把动作呈现为正在展开。

questions.question: have read 最突出什么关系？
questions.correct: 完成体把先前事件连接到现在观察点。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：完成体把先前事件连接到现在观察点。

narration.text:
时态不只是“现在、过去”的标签，更像摄像机站在哪里看事情；体则告诉你镜头里看到的是常态、正在进行，还是已经完成并和现在有关。<#0.9#>
先看，She lives in Shanghai now.<#0.7#>lives 把居住状态当作现在成立的事实，now 只是把语境说得更明确。<#0.8#>
再看，She is reading now.<#0.7#>is 负责现在时间，reading 把镜头拉到正在展开的过程，两部分缺一不可。<#0.8#>
最后看，I have read the book.<#0.7#>have read 把较早的阅读经历连到当前，重点不是过去日期，而是现在仍相关。<#0.9#>
先定观察点，再看动作内部状态。时间词只能提供线索，真正决定形式的是说话人想把事件放在哪个时间关系里。同一件事换一个观察点，形式也可能跟着变。

lessons.title: 一般体与进行体
lessons.meta: 整体事实与展开过程的对比
examples: Mia is staying with us this week.

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: boils 用一般现在时把“水在 100°C 沸腾”作为普遍规律，而不是某一刻正在发生的过程。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: is 承担现在时，staying 展示临时持续；this week 限定了这次暂住的时间范围。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: understand 在这里表示认知状态，直接用一般现在时；通常不把这种稳定状态写成正在进行。

rules: 一般现在时常表达习惯、规律、状态或长期事实。
进行体表达观察点附近正在展开或临时持续的活动。
状态动词通常不用进行体；若使用，往往表示临时行为或意义变化。

questions.question: 客观规律通常用什么？
questions.correct: 规律不强调临时展开过程。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：规律不强调临时展开过程。

questions.question: this week 的临时安排为何用 is staying？
questions.correct: 进行体把住宿看作当前临时过程。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：进行体把住宿看作当前临时过程。

questions.question: 哪句通常更自然？
questions.correct: understand 通常表示状态。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：understand 通常表示状态。

narration.text:
一般体和进行体的区别，可以先问：是在介绍一条稳定规律，还是把镜头对准一段正在展开、暂时持续的过程？不要见到 now 就机械加 doing。<#0.9#>
先看，Water boils at 100°C.<#0.7#>水在一百度沸腾是一条常规规律，不是在拍某一秒的过程，所以用 boils。<#0.8#>
再看，Mia is staying with us this week.<#0.7#>this week 限定一段临时时间，is staying 正好呈现这段暂住过程。<#0.8#>
最后看，I understand the rule.<#0.7#>understand 表示当前认知状态；这里不需要把“理解”硬说成正在展开的动作。<#0.9#>
先判断动作是常态、状态还是临时过程，再选一般体或进行体。像 understand 这样的状态意义，通常不会为了“此刻”就强行改成进行体。

lessons.title: 完成体与完成进行体
lessons.meta: 先前事件、当前结果与持续过程
examples: They have lived here for five years.
It has been raining all morning.

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: has lost 不只是报告过去“丢过”，还把结果连到现在：她现在没有钥匙或仍受影响。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: have lived 把居住状态从过去延续到现在，for five years 给出这段延续的总时长。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: has 承担现在时，been 建立完成，raining 建立进行；整条谓语突出雨从较早时间持续到现在。

rules: 现在完成体表示先前发生且与现在有关，不与明确结束的过去时间点连用。
since 给起点，for 给持续时长；延续性情形可连接过去与现在。
完成进行体突出从过去延续到观察点的过程或近期反复活动。

questions.question: has lost 在此暗示什么？
questions.correct: 完成体突出当前结果。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：完成体突出当前结果。

questions.question: for five years 表示什么？
questions.correct: for 后接一段时间。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：for 后接一段时间。

questions.question: has been raining 最突出什么？
questions.correct: have been doing 把过程延伸到现在。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：have been doing 把过程延伸到现在。

narration.text:
完成体像一座桥：动作可能发生在较早时间，但说话人关心它怎样连到现在；完成进行体还会把持续过程一起放到镜头里。<#0.9#>
先看，She has lost her key.<#0.7#>钥匙较早丢失，但句子关心她现在仍找不到或受到影响，所以使用 has lost。<#0.8#>
再看，They have lived here for five years.<#0.7#>居住从过去延续到现在，for five years 量出的是整段持续时间。<#0.8#>
最后看，It has been raining all morning.<#0.7#>雨从早些时候一直下到现在，has been raining 同时突出连接当前和持续过程。<#0.9#>
判断完成体时别只翻成“已经”。要问较早的事件给当前留下什么结果，或者从过去开始的状态、过程是否仍延续到观察点。

lessons.title: 将来表达与从句时间
lessons.meta: will、be going to、进行时及主将从现
examples: We are meeting the teacher tomorrow.
If it rains, we will stay home.

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: will 是限定情态助动词，answer 用原形；will answer 表示说话当下作出的即时决定。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: are 承担现在时，meeting 用进行体呈现已安排好的见面，tomorrow 把安排指向未来。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: 不是所有“将来意义”都在从句内使用 will。

rules: will 常表达即时决定、预测、承诺或中性将来。
be going to 常表达已有计划或有当前证据的预测；现在进行时可表达已安排事项。
时间、条件和让步从句表达将来时通常用一般现在时，主句再用将来表达。

questions.question: 听到电话后即时决定用什么？
questions.correct: 即时决定常用 will。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：即时决定常用 will。

questions.question: 已约好的明日见面可用什么？
questions.correct: 现在进行时可表示已安排将来。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：现在进行时可表示已安排将来。

questions.question: If it ___ tomorrow, we will stay home.
questions.correct: 条件从句表将来时用一般现在时。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：条件从句表将来时用一般现在时。

narration.text:
英语表达将来并不只有 will。临时决定、已经安排好的计划，以及条件成立后的结果，会选择不同结构；关键是先看说话场景。<#0.9#>
先看，I will answer the phone.<#0.7#>电话响起后当场决定去接，will answer 表达的正是说话时形成的决定。<#0.8#>
再看，We are meeting the teacher tomorrow.<#0.7#>见老师已经安排好，are meeting 用现在进行形式呈现确定安排，tomorrow 指向未来。<#0.8#>
最后看，If it rains, we will stay home.<#0.7#>if 从句先给未来条件，用 rains；主句再用 will stay 说明条件成立后的结果。<#0.9#>
先判断是当场决定、事先安排还是条件结果，再选择形式。尤其在 if 从句中，不要因为意义指向未来就把两个分句都塞进 will。

lessons.title: 主动与被动的视角
lessons.meta: 语态改变信息焦点，不改变事件角色
examples: The roof was damaged by the storm.

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: 主动句把原因来源 The storm 放在主语位置，damaged 直接指向承受影响的宾语 the roof。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: 被动句把承受影响的 roof 提到主语位置；was 承担过去时，damaged 用过去分词表达被动，by 短语补充施事来源。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: was stolen 已说明 bike 承受偷窃；不知道偷车者且他不是信息重点，因此无需添加空泛的 by someone。

rules: 主动句把施事者置于主语位置，被动句把动作承受者置于主语位置。
被动核心是相应时态的 be＋过去分词，原主动宾语变为主语。
施事未知、不重要或可由常识推断时，被动句通常省略 by 短语。

questions.question: 主动句主语 The storm 是什么角色？
questions.correct: 风暴导致损坏。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：风暴导致损坏。

questions.question: damaged the roof 转被动后 roof 变为什么？
questions.correct: 动作承受者提升为被动句主语。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：动作承受者提升为被动句主语。

questions.question: 为什么可不写 by someone？

options.text: 施事未知且不是信息重点

questions.correct: 被动允许 by 短语，但此处没有信息价值。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：被动允许 by 短语，但此处没有信息价值。

narration.text:
主动和被动不是把同一意思换个壳，而是把镜头对准不同角色：主动句先说谁造成动作，被动句先说谁受到影响。<#0.9#>
先看，The storm damaged the roof.<#0.7#>主动句先摆出 storm，让读者先看造成损坏的来源，再看到 roof 承受动作。<#0.8#>
再看，The roof was damaged by the storm.<#0.7#>被动句把 roof 推到句首；was damaged 说明它受到影响，by 短语才补回风暴。<#0.8#>
最后看，My bike was stolen.<#0.7#>自行车被偷已经是完整重点，偷车的人未知也不重要，没有必要虚加一个施事。<#0.9#>
先问主语是动作发出者还是承受者，再决定主动或被动。施事不知道、不重要或不想强调时，被动句不必硬加 by someone。镜头换了，事件中谁做、谁承受并没有改变。

lessons.title: 各时体中的被动链
lessons.meta: 改变最前面的限定助动词，保留 been/being 槽位
examples: The road is being repaired now.
The work has been finished already.

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: is 承担现在时并与 room 一致，cleaned 是过去分词；二者合成一般现在时被动谓语。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: is 承担现在时，being 建立进行，被动 be 再要求 repaired 用过去分词；整条链表示“正在被修”。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: has 承担现在时，been 是被动 be 在完成助动词后的形式，finished 用过去分词；整条链表达已完成的被动结果。

rules: 一般时被动用相应时态的 be＋过去分词。
进行体被动用 be＋being＋过去分词。
完成体被动用 have＋been＋过去分词。

questions.question: 一般现在被动结构是什么？
questions.correct: be 承担时态，过去分词表达被动。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：be 承担时态，过去分词表达被动。

questions.question: “正在被修”怎样表达？
questions.correct: 进行槽位 be doing 与被动槽位 be done 组合为 is being repaired。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：进行槽位 be doing 与被动槽位 be done 组合为 is being repaired。

questions.question: 完成被动结构是什么？
questions.correct: been 是被动 be 的过去分词，位于完成 have 后。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：been 是被动 be 的过去分词，位于完成 have 后。

narration.text:
被动可以出现在一般、进行和完成等不同时间画面里。看起来动词很多，其实只是在同一条谓语链上叠加“什么时候、怎样展开、谁承受动作”。<#0.9#>
先看，The room is cleaned daily.<#0.7#>is 负责现在和单数一致，cleaned 负责被动；daily 再说明这一动作的规律。<#0.8#>
再看，The road is being repaired now.<#0.7#>道路此刻处在维修过程中，所以进行层和被动层同时出现，形成 is being repaired。<#0.8#>
最后看，The work has been finished already.<#0.7#>工作已经完成，has been finished 把完成结果与被动关系叠在同一条链上。<#0.9#>
从左向右先找限定助动词，再识别进行或完成，最后确认被动结构落在过去分词上。每个形式只承担自己那一层信息。

lessons.title: 情态谓语系统
lessons.meta: 情态强度、时间推断与完成情态
examples: You must wear a seat belt.
She may have missed the train.

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: can 是本分句的限定情态词，承担可能/能力意义；swim 必须用原形，二者合成完整谓语。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: must 把说话者的强制立场加到 wear a seat belt 上；wear 用原形，must wear 是完整谓语核心。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: may 表示不确定推测，have missed 把推测指向较早发生的“错过”；整条链判断的是过去事件。

rules: 情态动词不加三单或时态词尾，后接动词原形。
must、should、may、might 等表达不同强度的义务、可能或判断，选择取决于语境立场。
情态词＋have＋过去分词把判断指向过去事件。

questions.question: She can ___ .
questions.correct: can 后用原形。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：can 后用原形。

questions.question: 强制义务最适合用什么？
questions.correct: must 表强义务。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：must 表强义务。

questions.question: may have missed 表示什么？

options.text: 对过去事件的可能推测

questions.correct: have missed 把情态判断指向先前事件。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：have missed 把情态判断指向先前事件。

narration.text:
情态动词像给动作加一层说话人的态度：能不能、必须不必须、可能不可能。它不替代动作，而是站在动作前面评价这件事。<#0.9#>
先看，She can swim.<#0.7#>can 先给 swim 加上能力意义，而真正动作仍由原形 swim 表达。<#0.8#>
再看，You must wear a seat belt.<#0.7#>must 把“系安全带”变成强义务；wear 不再自己变化。<#0.8#>
最后看，She may have missed the train.<#0.7#>may 表示不确定判断，have missed 把这个判断指向较早发生的误车。<#0.9#>
先确定情态意义，再看它判断的是现在动作还是较早事件。普通情态后接原形；情态加 have done 时，判断被推向过去。选词时还要比较语气强弱，“可能”和“必须”并不是同一种态度。

lessons.title: 否定与疑问的谓语操作
lessons.meta: 操作词承担 not、倒装与答语重复

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: 系动词 is 本身是限定操作词，not 直接跟在它后面；ready 是表语，因此不需要 does not be。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: 原句 arrived 没有助动词，疑问时加入 Did 并前移；过去标记转到 Did，arrive 恢复原形。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: Who 本身占主语位置，called 仍是一般过去时限定谓语；没有另一个主语需要和操作词倒装。

rules: be 作限定谓语时直接加 not，不使用 do。
一般疑问句把操作词移到主语前；若无操作词则加入 do。
特殊疑问词若本身作主语，不再进行主语—操作词倒装。

questions.question: Mia is ready 的否定是什么？
questions.correct: 限定 be 自己承担否定。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：限定 be 自己承担否定。

questions.question: They arrived on time 的疑问句为何用 arrive？

options.text: 过去标记已由 Did 承担

questions.correct: 一个分句的过去限定标记由操作词 did 表达。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：一个分句的过去限定标记由操作词 did 表达。

questions.question: 哪句询问“谁给你打电话”？
questions.correct: Who 本身就是主语，通常不用 do。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：Who 本身就是主语，通常不用 do。

narration.text:
否定和疑问看似要改整句，其实核心动作只有一个：找到限定操作词。它负责接 not，也负责在一般疑问句里移动到主语前。<#0.9#>
先看，Mia is not ready.<#0.7#>is 本身就能接 not，ready 只是表语，因此不用额外增加 do。<#0.8#>
再看，Did they arrive on time?<#0.7#>原句没有助动词，Did 被请到句首承担过去和疑问，arrive 随即恢复原形。<#0.8#>
最后看，Who called you?<#0.7#>Who 就是要寻找的主语，called 直接跟在后面；这里没有另一个主语需要倒装。<#0.9#>
变句前先找 be、助动词或情态词；都没有才用 do 支持。特殊疑问词本身作主语时，不要再多做一次倒装。每次只让一个词承担限定变化，实义动词就不会又变一次。先找开关，再变句。

lessons.title: 强调 do
lessons.meta: 在肯定句中加强确认、对比或反驳

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: 肯定句加入 do，不改变“理解”的事件，只加强“我确实理解”的确认或反驳语气。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: does 同时承担强调、现在时和三单一致，所以后面的实义动词必须是原形 want。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: did 同时承担强调和过去时，所以 call 不再使用过去式；did call 合起来表示“昨天确实打了”。

rules: 肯定陈述句可用 do/does/did＋原形强调真实性。
强调 do 承担时态和一致，后面的实义动词使用原形。
强调过去事实用 did＋原形，而不是 did＋过去式。

questions.question: I do understand 中 do 的作用是什么？
questions.correct: 肯定句中的 do 提供强调。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：肯定句中的 do 提供强调。

questions.question: 哪句正确？
questions.correct: 三单标记在 does 上，want 用原形。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：三单标记在 does 上，want 用原形。

questions.question: “他昨天确实打了电话”怎样表达？
questions.correct: 过去标记由 did 承担。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：过去标记由 did 承担。

narration.text:
肯定句里出现 do、does 或 did，有时不是提问，也不是否定，而是在说“确实如此”。它常用来确认事实、纠正别人或加强对比。<#0.9#>
先看，I do understand you.<#0.7#>do 没有改变 understand 的动作，只把语气加强成“我确实理解”。<#0.8#>
再看，She does want to help.<#0.7#>does 同时扛起强调和三单，want 不能再加 s，否则同一变化会出现两次。<#0.8#>
最后看，He did call yesterday.<#0.7#>过去的强调由 did 负责，所以后面保留 call，而不是再写过去式。<#0.9#>
强调 do 自己承担时态和主谓一致，后面的实义动词必须保持原形。听语气时抓住“确实”，写形式时避免重复变化。句子仍然是肯定陈述，只是说话人把语气特别加重了。

lessons.title: 短答与谓语替代
lessons.meta: 保留操作词，避免重复整个谓语
examples: Has Mia left? Yes, she has.
Mia sings better than Tom does.
Mia can swim, and so can Tom.

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: 原问句的第一个助动词是 Has，短答保留同一个操作词，并把主语 Mia 换成 she：Yes, she has。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: than 分句中的 does 保留现在时和与 Tom 的一致，同时替代前文完整谓语 sings，避免重复。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: 前句完整谓语是 can swim，so can Tom 保留相同情态操作词 can，并省去重复的 swim。

rules: 一般疑问句短答重复操作词，并与答语主语一致。
do/does/did 可替代前文的一般时实义谓语，避免重复。
so/neither＋操作词＋主语可表达“也如此/也不如此”，操作词取决于前句谓语。

questions.question: Has Mia left? 的肯定短答是什么？
questions.correct: 原问句操作词是 has。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：原问句操作词是 has。

questions.question: Tom does 中 does 替代什么？
questions.correct: does 代替重复谓语 sings。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：does 代替重复谓语 sings。

questions.question: Mia can swim. Tom 也会。应说什么？
questions.correct: 前句操作词是 can。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：前句操作词是 can。

narration.text:
英语短答不喜欢把刚说过的整条谓语再念一遍，会留下一个能代表原结构的操作词。比较句和“也一样”结构也使用同样办法。<#0.9#>
先看，Has Mia left? Yes, she has.<#0.7#>问句使用 Has，答语就保留 has；Mia 换成 she 后，不需要再重复 left。<#0.8#>
再看，Mia sings better than Tom does.<#0.7#>does 在比较分句里代替 sings，同时与 Tom 保持现在时和单数一致。<#0.8#>
最后看，Mia can swim, and so can Tom.<#0.7#>前句的关键操作词是 can，所以“Tom 也会”仍保留 can，而不是换成 does。<#0.9#>
先回到前一句找操作词：has 就保留 has，can 就保留 can，一般实义动词则用 do、does 或 did 替代。不要只按中文的“也”来猜。

groups.title: 进阶挑战 · 5 节
groups.copy: 处理意义一致、过去序列、半情态、共享省略与综合链条。

lessons.title: 就近一致与意义一致
lessons.meta: 形式规则之外还要看连接方式和整体意义
examples: Either Mia or the boys are coming.
Half of the water is gone.

analyses.label: 现在分词（与 are 构成谓语）

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: either...or 连接两个主语时看靠近谓语的一项；boys 离 are 最近且为复数，所以用 are。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: Ten minutes 形式上有复数 -s，但这里表示一个整体时长，所以限定系动词用单数 is。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: Half of 本身不决定单复数；of 后的 water 是不可数名词，所以限定谓语用 is。

rules: either...or、neither...nor、not only...but also 连接主语时通常按就近原则。
时间、距离、金额作为一个整体量时通常用单数谓语。
分数、百分数或 some/most/all + of 的一致通常看 of 后名词。

questions.question: Either Mia or the boys ___ coming.
questions.correct: 较近主语 boys 是复数。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：较近主语 boys 是复数。

questions.question: Ten minutes ___ enough.
questions.correct: 十分钟在此被看作一个整体时长。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：十分钟在此被看作一个整体时长。

questions.question: Half of the students ___ ready.
questions.correct: of 后 students 为复数。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：of 后 students 为复数。

narration.text:
有些主语不能只数词尾，还要看连接方式和整句话把它当成一个整体还是多个个体。这一课处理的就是基础一致之外的两类特殊判断。<#0.9#>
先看，Either Mia or the boys are coming.<#0.7#>either...or 让谓语看靠近的一项；这里 boys 紧挨谓语，所以选择 are。<#0.8#>
再看，Ten minutes is enough.<#0.7#>ten minutes 虽有复数形式，这里却被当作一整段时长，搭配单数 is。<#0.8#>
最后看，Half of the water is gone.<#0.7#>half 本身不决定形式；water 是不可数整体，所以这一句仍用 is。<#0.9#>
判断顺序是：先看有没有 either...or 一类连接；再找靠近谓语的主语；如果表示时间、金额或比例，再看语境把它理解成整体还是成员。

lessons.title: 过去时间序列
lessons.meta: 以过去观察点排列先后与持续
examples: The train had left before we arrived.
I was cooking when he called.

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: rang 用一般过去时，把八点响铃作为过去时间线上的主要事件。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: arrived 是过去参照点，had left 把火车离开定位在这个参照点之前。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: was cooking 是当时正在展开的背景过程，called 是插入这个背景的较短事件。

rules: 一般过去时叙述过去观察点上的主要事件。
过去完成体表示在另一个过去事件之前已经发生。
过去进行体提供过去某时正在展开的背景，常与一般过去时的插入事件对照。

questions.question: 明确过去时间 at eight 对应什么？
questions.correct: 结束的过去时间通常用一般过去时。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：结束的过去时间通常用一般过去时。

questions.question: 哪个动作更早？
questions.correct: 过去完成体标记“过去的过去”。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：过去完成体标记“过去的过去”。

questions.question: 哪个是背景过程？
questions.correct: 过去进行体呈现展开中的背景。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：过去进行体呈现展开中的背景。

narration.text:
讲过去不只需要“过去式”，还要把几件事排出先后和背景。可以把时间线画出来：哪件事是参照点，哪件更早，哪件当时正在进行。<#0.9#>
先看，The bell rang at eight.<#0.7#>八点是明确的过去时间点，rang 直接把响铃事件放到这条过去时间线上。<#0.8#>
再看，The train had left before we arrived.<#0.7#>arrived 提供较晚的参照点，火车离开更早，因此用 had left 拉开先后。<#0.8#>
最后看，I was cooking when he called.<#0.7#>做饭是当时铺开的背景，来电是插入背景的短事件，两种过去形式分工不同。<#0.9#>
先找到过去参照点；更早完成的用过去完成，当时展开的背景用过去进行，落在时间线上的主要事件用一般过去。先后清楚，时态才不会打架。

lessons.title: 半情态与边界形式
lessons.meta: have to、be able to、used to 等兼具词汇和助动特征
examples: She has been able to solve it.
Did you use to live here?

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: have to 像实义结构一样需要 Do 来形成一般现在时疑问；限定标记在 Do 上，have 和 leave 都用原形。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: has 是限定完成助动词，been 是 be 的过去分词，able to solve 是其表语内容；不要把 able 当成助动词。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: used to 本来表示过去习惯；变疑问后过去标记由 Did 承担，因此 used 恢复为 use。

rules: have to 表外部义务，疑问否定通常需要 do 支持。
be able to 可进入更多时态和非谓语位置，be 承担限定变化。
used to 表过去习惯或状态；否定和疑问常用 did，used 恢复 use。

questions.question: have to 的一般现在疑问句用什么操作词？

options.text: 直接把 have 前移总是正确

questions.correct: 现代英语通常用 do you have to。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：现代英语通常用 do you have to。

questions.question: has been able to 中哪个部分承担完成时？
questions.correct: have＋been 构成完成链。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：have＋been 构成完成链。

questions.question: 规范疑问结构是哪一个？
questions.correct: 过去标记由 did 承担，use 用原形。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：过去标记由 did 承担，use 用原形。

narration.text:
have to、able 结构和 used to 意思有点像情态，但语法行为又保留了实义结构的特点，所以不能全部照 can、must 的方法处理。<#0.9#>
先看，Do you have to leave?<#0.7#>have to 自己不能像 must 那样直接前移，这里需要 Do 来承担疑问。<#0.8#>
再看，She has been able to solve it.<#0.7#>完成变化落在 has been 上，able to solve 说明到现在已经具备的能力。<#0.8#>
最后看，Did you use to live here?<#0.7#>Did 已经带走过去标记，后面只能写 use to，不能再让 used 重复过去变化。<#0.9#>
先找真正承担时态和疑问操作的词。半情态的意义可以整体理解，但变否定、疑问或完成时，仍要按它内部的动词结构变化。

lessons.title: 谓语共享与省略
lessons.meta: 还原平行项中的共同助动词或谓语
examples: Mia has finished the report and sent it.
Mia can play the piano, and Tom can, too.
Some reports were accepted, but others were not.

analyses.label: 共享 has 的并列谓语
省略 play the piano 的分句

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: has 同时管 finished 和 sent，可还原为 has finished... and has sent...；两个实义动词并列，共享一个完成助动词。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: 第二分句保留 can 来表示同样的情态和时态关系，play the piano 可从前句准确恢复，所以省略。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: others were not 保留被动操作词 were 和否定 not，accepted 可从前一分句恢复；省略后语态关系仍清楚。

rules: 并列谓语可以共享同一个主语和助动词。
助动词后的共同实义谓语可在第二并列项中省略，但意义由平行结构恢复。
省略必须保持时态、语态和情态关系可恢复；不清楚时应保留完整谓语。

questions.question: sent it 与哪个助动词共享完成结构？
questions.correct: 可还原为 has finished and has sent。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：可还原为 has finished and has sent。

questions.question: Tom can, too 中省略什么？
questions.correct: 操作词 can 保留并替代完整谓语。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：操作词 can 保留并替代完整谓语。

questions.question: others were not 中省略什么？
questions.correct: 被动操作词 were 保留，过去分词由前项恢复。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：被动操作词 were 保留，过去分词由前项恢复。

narration.text:
并列结构里，相同的信息可以只说一次。看见后半句变短时，不要认为它缺语法成分，而要从前面的平行结构把共享或省略的部分还原出来。<#0.9#>
先看，Mia has finished the report and sent it.<#0.7#>has 同时管 finished 和 sent，两个动作并列共享同一层完成意义。<#0.8#>
再看，Mia can play the piano, and Tom can, too.<#0.7#>Tom 后只留下 can，读者能从前半句恢复 play the piano，所以无需重复。<#0.8#>
最后看，Some reports were accepted, but others were not.<#0.7#>were not 保留被动和否定，省掉的 accepted 能从前一分句唯一找回。<#0.9#>
还原后要检查时态、语态和情态是否仍一致。能唯一恢复才可以省；如果读者可能恢复出不同内容，就应该保留完整谓语。

lessons.title: 综合谓语分析
lessons.meta: 按限定性、链条、时体、语态、情态和一致逐层检查
examples: The road may have been closed.
The work must have been completed.

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: may 是唯一限定操作词，have 建立完成，been closed 建立被动；从左到右是一条完整谓语链。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: must 表说话者判断，have 把事件放在较早时间，been completed 表被动；主语 work 是完成动作的承受者。

exampleNotes.title: 例句说明
exampleNotes.body: 检查顺序：主语 → 限定操作词 → 助动词链 → 实义动词 → 补足成分。

rules: 复杂谓语先找第一个限定操作词，再按助动词槽位向右分析。
判断谓语意义时分别回答：观察点何时、事件怎样展开、主语是施事还是承受者、说话者态度如何。
最终检查主语一致和操作规则：限定标记只出现一次，后续动词形式由前一助动词决定。

questions.question: may have been closed 的限定操作词是什么？
questions.correct: 最前面的情态词承担限定性。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：最前面的情态词承担限定性。

questions.question: must have been completed 包含哪些系统？
questions.correct: must 表判断，have 表完成，been completed 表被动。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：must 表判断，have 表完成，been completed 表被动。

questions.question: 为什么不能说 Does the plan seems...?

options.text: 三单限定标记已在 Does 上

questions.correct: 同一分句不能在 Does 和 seems 上重复三单标记。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：同一分句不能在 Does 和 seems 上重复三单标记。

narration.text:
面对长谓语，最稳的方法不是一次翻完，而是像拆积木一样分层：谁承担限定性，后面依次加入了什么时间、语态和情态信息。<#0.9#>
先看，The road may have been closed.<#0.7#>may 是最左边的限定开关，have 加入完成，been closed 再加入被动。<#0.8#>
再看，The work must have been completed.<#0.7#>must 先表达判断，have 把完成放到较早时间，been completed 表明 work 承受动作。<#0.8#>
最后看，Does the plan seem reasonable?<#0.7#>Does 已经承担现在时和三单，seem 必须用原形；reasonable 再说明 plan 的状态。<#0.9#>
综合判断按固定顺序走：主语、限定操作词、助动词链、实义动词、补足成分。每层只标一次，既不会漏，也不会把多个形式误数成多个谓语。

en.title: Predicate system · 20 lessons
en.copy: Start with finiteness, then build agreement, tense-aspect, voice, modality and clause operations.

course.title: Definition and finite core of predicates
course.meta: Find the tense- or modal-bearing core of each clause

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: works is the only verb marked for present tense and agreement with Mia, so it is the finite predicate.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: wants carries present tense and is finite; to leave has no tense and fills the object slot after wants.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: At the outer level, know is the main-clause finite predicate; she agrees has its own predicate inside the that-clause.

rules: A finite predicate carries tense or modality and has a syntactic relation with its subject.
A non-finite form cannot alone form the finite predicate of an independent clause.
Each clause in a complex sentence has its own finite predicate; do not merge a subordinate predicate into the main predicate.

questions.question: Which word is the finite predicate?
questions.correct: works carries present tense and agrees with Mia.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: works carries present tense and agrees with Mia.

questions.question: What is the finite predicate?
questions.correct: to leave has no tense; wants is finite.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: to leave has no tense; wants is finite.

questions.question: What is the main-clause predicate?
questions.correct: agrees belongs inside the that-clause; know is the outer predicate.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: agrees belongs inside the that-clause; know is the outer predicate.

narration.text:
一句话里出现几个动词，不等于就有几个谓语。先找哪一个动词在负责整句话的时间、语气和主语变化，它像开关一样让一个小句真正成立。这个核心叫限定谓语。<#0.8#>
Mia works here。<#0.8#>Mia 是主语，works 一边说“工作”，一边把事情放在一般现在时，还和单数主语 Mia 对应。here 只补充工作地点，不属于谓语核心。<#0.8#>
Mia wants to leave。<#0.8#>这里有 wants 和 leave 两个动作意思，但只有 wants 在承担主句的时间和主语变化。to leave 只补充“想做什么”，自己不让主句成立，所以它是非谓语部分。看到两个动词形式，不能直接画成两个谓语。<#0.8#>
I know that she agrees。<#0.8#>先看外层，I 的限定谓语是 know。that 后面又有一套“谁怎么样”：she 是从句主语，agrees 是从句自己的限定谓语。这里确实有两个限定谓语，因为句中包含两个小句。<#0.8#>
判断时先划分小句；再在每个小句里找负责时间、语气或主语变化的动词；如果它后面还跟着其他动词形式，再把相关部分合成完整谓语。先分层，再数谓语，最不容易错。

course.title: Order in the auxiliary chain
course.meta: Modal, perfect, progressive and passive occupy fixed slots
examples: The bridge may have been repaired.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: may carries finiteness and modality, while begin stays in the base form; together may begin is the complete predicate.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: may is the finite modal, have builds the perfect, and been waiting builds the progressive; all four words form one complete predicate.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: may marks possibility, have marks perfect aspect, and been repaired marks passive voice; they form one auxiliary chain, not three predicates.

rules: A modal comes first in the auxiliary chain and takes a base form.
Perfect have follows a modal and precedes progressive or passive be.
The full template is modal + perfect + progressive + passive + lexical verb, using only needed slots.

questions.question: What follows may?
questions.correct: A modal takes base-form begin.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: A modal takes base-form begin.

questions.question: Which order is correct?
questions.correct: The order is modal + perfect + progressive + lexical verb.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The order is modal + perfect + progressive + lexical verb.

questions.question: What does may have been repaired combine?
questions.correct: may marks modality; have been builds a perfect passive.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: may marks modality; have been builds a perfect passive.

narration.text:
把一串助动词想成排队上车：谁站前面、谁站后面都有固定位置，不能随意换座。先抓住情态、完成、进行和被动这四层，长谓语就不会乱。<#0.9#>
先看，The work may begin soon.<#0.7#>may 先把整件事标成“可能”，begin 保持原形，两个词合起来才说完整。<#0.8#>
再看，She may have been waiting.<#0.7#>这次链条比第一句多了完成和进行：先是 may，再是 have，最后落到 been waiting。<#0.8#>
最后看，The bridge may have been repaired.<#0.7#>第三句没有进行这一层，may、have 和 been repaired 分别交代可能、较早完成和被动。<#0.9#>
遇到长谓语，从最左边开始读：先判断情态，再看完成、进行或被动，最后落到实义动作。缺哪层就跳过哪层，但顺序不能倒。

course.title: The predicate operator
course.meta: The first auxiliary carries question, negation and inversion operations

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: The first auxiliary has moves before she to carry the question operation; has finished still forms the perfect predicate.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: has is first in the auxiliary chain, so not follows it; has not finished is the complete negative predicate.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: Statement Mia likes tea → question Does Mia like tea?

rules: When an auxiliary is present, the first auxiliary carries inversion and moves before the subject.
When an auxiliary is present, not follows the first auxiliary.
When a simple-tense lexical verb has no auxiliary, do/does/did supplies the operator and the lexical verb returns to base form.

questions.question: How does the question from She has finished begin?
questions.correct: Move existing first auxiliary has forward.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Move existing first auxiliary has forward.

questions.question: Where should not go?
questions.correct: The first auxiliary has carries negation.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The first auxiliary has carries negation.

questions.question: Which is correct?
questions.correct: Does carries agreement; like returns to base form.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Does carries agreement; like returns to base form.

narration.text:
一句话要变成疑问或否定，通常不是整条谓语一起搬家，而是让最前面的助动词当“操作开关”。先找到这个开关，后面的变化会简单很多。<#0.9#>
先看，Has she finished?<#0.7#>原陈述句已经有 has，所以直接把它移到 she 前面，不需要另找帮手。<#0.8#>
再看，She has not finished.<#0.7#>变否定时 has 不搬家，not 紧跟在它后面，finished 继续保留过去分词。<#0.8#>
最后看，Does Mia like tea?<#0.7#>likes 原来独自承担三单；变疑问后这份变化交给 Does，like 就回到原形。<#0.9#>
做变句题时先问：原句有没有现成助动词？有，就操作第一个；没有，再请 do、does 或 did 来帮忙，并让实义动词回到原形。这样疑问、否定和时态都会落在同一个开关上。

course.title: Basic subject–verb agreement
course.meta: The finite verb agrees with the subject in person and number

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: The subject head boy is third-person singular, so finite plays carries -s for agreement.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: Present-tense be agrees with I as am; ready is the subject complement and does not control agreement.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: Tom and Mia are two separate people joined as a plural subject, so finite linking be is are.

rules: In the present simple, a third-person singular subject takes the corresponding singular verb.
Forms of be directly reflect the subject’s person, number and time.
Two independent subjects joined by and normally form a plural subject.

questions.question: The boy ___ football.
questions.correct: The head subject boy is third-person singular.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The head subject boy is third-person singular.

questions.question: I ___ ready.
questions.correct: First-person singular present uses am.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: First-person singular present uses am.

questions.question: Tom and Mia ___ ready.
questions.correct: Two coordinated subjects take a plural verb.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Two coordinated subjects take a plural verb.

narration.text:
主谓一致可以先理解成“主语和限定动词要对上号”。现在时里，主语是一个人、两个人，或者是 I，动词给出的形式会不同。<#0.9#>
先看，The boy plays football.<#0.7#>boy 只表示一个第三人称对象，所以现在时的 play 要带上 s。<#0.8#>
再看，I am ready.<#0.7#>主语换成 I，be 就使用 am；ready 只是说明状态，不参与选择。<#0.8#>
最后看，Tom and Mia are ready.<#0.7#>Tom 和 Mia 被 and 连成两个人，主语按复数理解，因此使用 are。<#0.9#>
先圈完整主语，再判断它的人称和单复数，最后只检查限定谓语。表语、宾语和地点说明都不决定这次变化。简单句先把“谁”和“怎么样”对好，不要看见一个名词就去改动词。先确定主语范围，再动谓语。

course.title: Finding the head in a complex subject
course.meta: Postmodifiers do not change the number of the subject head
examples: The box of books is heavy.
Mia, together with her friends, is here.
She is one of the students who work hard.

analyses.text: She is one of the students
analyses.label: Main clause

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: The full subject is The box of books, but its head is singular box; of books only postmodifies it, so the verb is is.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: together with her friends is an added modifier, not an and-coordinate subject; the finite verb still agrees with Mia as is.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: The outer core is She is one of the students; inside the relative clause, who refers to plural students, so its finite verb is work.

rules: When an of- or with-phrase modifies the subject, agreement follows the preceding head.
together with, as well as and along with introduce additions, not an and-type plural subject.
A verb in a relative clause agrees with the antecedent represented by the relative word.

questions.question: The box of books ___ heavy.
questions.correct: The head box is singular.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The head box is singular.

questions.question: Mia, together with her friends, ___ here.
questions.correct: The subject head remains Mia.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The subject head remains Mia.

questions.question: Why is work used after who?
questions.correct: The relative word refers to students inside the clause.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The relative word refers to students inside the clause.

narration.text:
主语一长，最容易被离动词最近的复数词带跑。正确做法像拆快递：先去掉外面的补充说明，找到真正决定单复数的中心词。<#0.9#>
先看，The box of books is heavy.<#0.7#>books 虽然靠近 is，却只是放在 of 后修饰 box；真正管单复数的是 box。<#0.8#>
再看，Mia, together with her friends, is here.<#0.7#>friends 也只是附加说明，核心主语仍是 Mia，所以不能被复数词带成 are。<#0.8#>
最后看，She is one of the students who work hard.<#0.7#>这一句要进入 who 从句判断：who 指回 students，从句里的 work 因此按复数处理。<#0.9#>
看到 of、with、together with 或关系从句时，先划清它们属于哪一层。限定谓语跟真正的主语中心一致，不是机械跟最近的名词一致。

course.title: Proximity and notional agreement
course.meta: Beyond form, consider coordination and meaning
examples: Either Mia or the boys are coming.
Half of the water is gone.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: With either...or subjects, agreement follows the nearer item; plural boys is nearest, so the verb is are.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: Ten minutes is plural in form but denotes one duration here, so finite linking be is singular is.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: Half of does not decide number by itself; water after of is uncountable, so the finite verb is is.

rules: With either...or, neither...nor and not only...but also subjects, agreement normally follows the nearer subject.
A period, distance or sum treated as one unit normally takes a singular verb.
Agreement with fractions, percentages or some/most/all + of normally follows the of-noun.

questions.question: Either Mia or the boys ___ coming.
questions.correct: The nearer subject boys is plural.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The nearer subject boys is plural.

questions.question: Ten minutes ___ enough.
questions.correct: Ten minutes is treated as one duration.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Ten minutes is treated as one duration.

questions.question: Half of the students ___ ready.
questions.correct: Agreement follows plural students.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Agreement follows plural students.

narration.text:
有些主语不能只数词尾，还要看连接方式和整句话把它当成一个整体还是多个个体。这一课处理的就是基础一致之外的两类特殊判断。<#0.9#>
先看，Either Mia or the boys are coming.<#0.7#>either...or 让谓语看靠近的一项；这里 boys 紧挨谓语，所以选择 are。<#0.8#>
再看，Ten minutes is enough.<#0.7#>ten minutes 虽有复数形式，这里却被当作一整段时长，搭配单数 is。<#0.8#>
最后看，Half of the water is gone.<#0.7#>half 本身不决定形式；water 是不可数整体，所以这一句仍用 is。<#0.9#>
判断顺序是：先看有没有 either...or 一类连接；再找靠近谓语的主语；如果表示时间、金额或比例，再看语境把它理解成整体还是成员。

course.title: Time relations in tense and aspect
course.meta: Tense locates the viewpoint; aspect presents the event internally

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: Present-tense lives locates the viewpoint now and presents the residence as currently true; now only confirms the context.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: is carries present tense and reading presents an unfolding process; together is reading is one present-progressive predicate.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: have carries present tense and read presents a prior event; have read links that event to a result or experience relevant now.

rules: Tense first locates the viewpoint in present or past; time words are clues, while context determines the relation.
Aspect is not time: progressive presents an unfolding process; perfect presents prior occurrence relevant to the viewpoint.
The same event may take different aspect depending on how the speaker chooses to view it.

questions.question: Where does lives locate the viewpoint?
questions.correct: Present simple locates the viewpoint in the present.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Present simple locates the viewpoint in the present.

questions.question: What does progressive aspect highlight?
questions.correct: is reading presents the event as unfolding.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: is reading presents the event as unfolding.

questions.question: What relation does have read highlight?
questions.correct: The perfect links a prior event to the present viewpoint.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The perfect links a prior event to the present viewpoint.

narration.text:
时态不只是“现在、过去”的标签，更像摄像机站在哪里看事情；体则告诉你镜头里看到的是常态、正在进行，还是已经完成并和现在有关。<#0.9#>
先看，She lives in Shanghai now.<#0.7#>lives 把居住状态当作现在成立的事实，now 只是把语境说得更明确。<#0.8#>
再看，She is reading now.<#0.7#>is 负责现在时间，reading 把镜头拉到正在展开的过程，两部分缺一不可。<#0.8#>
最后看，I have read the book.<#0.7#>have read 把较早的阅读经历连到当前，重点不是过去日期，而是现在仍相关。<#0.9#>
先定观察点，再看动作内部状态。时间词只能提供线索，真正决定形式的是说话人想把事件放在哪个时间关系里。同一件事换一个观察点，形式也可能跟着变。

course.title: Simple and progressive aspect
course.meta: Whole facts versus unfolding processes
examples: Mia is staying with us this week.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: boils uses the present simple to present a general truth, not a process unfolding at one moment.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: is carries present tense and staying presents a temporary ongoing situation; this week sets its limited time frame.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: understand denotes a cognitive state here, so the present simple is natural rather than a progressive process.

rules: Present simple commonly expresses habits, general truths, states or lasting facts.
Progressive aspect expresses an activity unfolding around the viewpoint or continuing temporarily.
Stative verbs normally avoid progressive aspect; when used, they often express temporary behaviour or a changed meaning.

questions.question: What normally expresses a general truth?
questions.correct: A general truth is not presented as a temporary process.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: A general truth is not presented as a temporary process.

questions.question: Why is is staying used for this week?
questions.correct: The progressive presents the stay as temporary and current.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The progressive presents the stay as temporary and current.

questions.question: Which is normally more natural?
questions.correct: understand is normally stative.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: understand is normally stative.

narration.text:
一般体和进行体的区别，可以先问：是在介绍一条稳定规律，还是把镜头对准一段正在展开、暂时持续的过程？不要见到 now 就机械加 doing。<#0.9#>
先看，Water boils at 100°C.<#0.7#>水在一百度沸腾是一条常规规律，不是在拍某一秒的过程，所以用 boils。<#0.8#>
再看，Mia is staying with us this week.<#0.7#>this week 限定一段临时时间，is staying 正好呈现这段暂住过程。<#0.8#>
最后看，I understand the rule.<#0.7#>understand 表示当前认知状态；这里不需要把“理解”硬说成正在展开的动作。<#0.9#>
先判断动作是常态、状态还是临时过程，再选一般体或进行体。像 understand 这样的状态意义，通常不会为了“此刻”就强行改成进行体。

course.title: Perfect and perfect progressive
course.meta: Prior event, current relevance and continuing process
examples: They have lived here for five years.
It has been raining all morning.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: has lost does more than report a past event; it links the loss to the present result that she lacks the key or is still affected.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: have lived extends the residence from the past to now, and for five years gives its duration.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: has carries present tense, been builds the perfect, and raining builds the progressive; the whole predicate highlights a process continuing to now.

rules: Present perfect expresses a prior event relevant now and does not normally combine with a definite finished past time.
since gives a starting point and for gives duration; continuing situations can link past and present.
Perfect progressive highlights a process continuing to the viewpoint or repeated recently.

questions.question: What does has lost imply here?
questions.correct: The perfect highlights a current result.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The perfect highlights a current result.

questions.question: What does for five years express?
questions.correct: for introduces a duration.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: for introduces a duration.

questions.question: What does has been raining emphasize?
questions.correct: have been doing extends the process to now.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: have been doing extends the process to now.

narration.text:
完成体像一座桥：动作可能发生在较早时间，但说话人关心它怎样连到现在；完成进行体还会把持续过程一起放到镜头里。<#0.9#>
先看，She has lost her key.<#0.7#>钥匙较早丢失，但句子关心她现在仍找不到或受到影响，所以使用 has lost。<#0.8#>
再看，They have lived here for five years.<#0.7#>居住从过去延续到现在，for five years 量出的是整段持续时间。<#0.8#>
最后看，It has been raining all morning.<#0.7#>雨从早些时候一直下到现在，has been raining 同时突出连接当前和持续过程。<#0.9#>
判断完成体时别只翻成“已经”。要问较早的事件给当前留下什么结果，或者从过去开始的状态、过程是否仍延续到观察点。

course.title: Sequencing past events
course.meta: Ordering prior events around a past viewpoint
examples: The train had left before we arrived.
I was cooking when he called.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: rang uses the past simple to place the bell event on the past timeline at eight.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: arrived supplies the past reference point, and had left places the departure before it.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: was cooking is the unfolding background process, while called is the shorter event that occurs within it.

rules: Past simple narrates the main event at a past viewpoint.
Past perfect marks an event completed before another past event.
Past progressive provides an unfolding past background, often contrasted with an interrupting past-simple event.

questions.question: What fits the definite past time at eight?
questions.correct: A finished past time normally takes past simple.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: A finished past time normally takes past simple.

questions.question: Which event happened earlier?
questions.correct: Past perfect marks an earlier past.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Past perfect marks an earlier past.

questions.question: Which is the background process?
questions.correct: Past progressive presents the unfolding background.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Past progressive presents the unfolding background.

narration.text:
讲过去不只需要“过去式”，还要把几件事排出先后和背景。可以把时间线画出来：哪件事是参照点，哪件更早，哪件当时正在进行。<#0.9#>
先看，The bell rang at eight.<#0.7#>八点是明确的过去时间点，rang 直接把响铃事件放到这条过去时间线上。<#0.8#>
再看，The train had left before we arrived.<#0.7#>arrived 提供较晚的参照点，火车离开更早，因此用 had left 拉开先后。<#0.8#>
最后看，I was cooking when he called.<#0.7#>做饭是当时铺开的背景，来电是插入背景的短事件，两种过去形式分工不同。<#0.9#>
先找到过去参照点；更早完成的用过去完成，当时展开的背景用过去进行，落在时间线上的主要事件用一般过去。先后清楚，时态才不会打架。

course.title: Future expressions and clause time
course.meta: will, be going to, progressive arrangements and present in future clauses
examples: We are meeting the teacher tomorrow.
If it rains, we will stay home.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: will is the finite modal auxiliary and answer stays in the base form; will answer expresses a decision made at speaking time.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: are carries present tense, meeting presents an arranged meeting, and tomorrow locates that arrangement in the future.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: Not every future meaning uses will inside the subordinate clause.

rules: will commonly expresses a spontaneous decision, prediction, promise or neutral future.
be going to commonly expresses a prior plan or evidence-based prediction; present progressive can express a fixed arrangement.
Future time, condition and concession clauses normally use present simple while the main clause carries future marking.

questions.question: What expresses a spontaneous decision on hearing the phone?
questions.correct: will commonly marks a spontaneous decision.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: will commonly marks a spontaneous decision.

questions.question: What can express a fixed meeting tomorrow?
questions.correct: Present progressive can mark a future arrangement.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Present progressive can mark a future arrangement.

questions.question: If it ___ tomorrow, we will stay home.
questions.correct: Use present simple in the future condition clause.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use present simple in the future condition clause.

narration.text:
英语表达将来并不只有 will。临时决定、已经安排好的计划，以及条件成立后的结果，会选择不同结构；关键是先看说话场景。<#0.9#>
先看，I will answer the phone.<#0.7#>电话响起后当场决定去接，will answer 表达的正是说话时形成的决定。<#0.8#>
再看，We are meeting the teacher tomorrow.<#0.7#>见老师已经安排好，are meeting 用现在进行形式呈现确定安排，tomorrow 指向未来。<#0.8#>
最后看，If it rains, we will stay home.<#0.7#>if 从句先给未来条件，用 rains；主句再用 will stay 说明条件成立后的结果。<#0.9#>
先判断是当场决定、事先安排还是条件结果，再选择形式。尤其在 if 从句中，不要因为意义指向未来就把两个分句都塞进 will。

course.title: Active and passive viewpoint
course.meta: Voice changes information focus, not event roles
examples: The roof was damaged by the storm.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: The active clause puts the cause The storm in subject position, and damaged points to the affected object the roof.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: The passive promotes affected roof to subject; was carries past tense, damaged marks passive voice, and the by-phrase adds the agent.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: was stolen already presents bike as affected; the thief is unknown and not the focus, so a vague by someone adds nothing.

rules: Active voice places the agent as subject; passive voice places the affected participant as subject.
The passive core is the relevant form of be + past participle; the active object becomes subject.
The by-phrase is normally omitted when the agent is unknown, unimportant or obvious.

questions.question: What semantic role does The storm have?
questions.correct: The storm causes the damage.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The storm causes the damage.

questions.question: What does roof become in the passive?
questions.correct: The affected participant becomes passive subject.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The affected participant becomes passive subject.

questions.question: Why can by someone be omitted?

options.text: The agent is unknown and not the focus
Passives can never name an agent

questions.correct: A passive permits a by-phrase, but it adds no useful information here.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: A passive permits a by-phrase, but it adds no useful information here.

narration.text:
主动和被动不是把同一意思换个壳，而是把镜头对准不同角色：主动句先说谁造成动作，被动句先说谁受到影响。<#0.9#>
先看，The storm damaged the roof.<#0.7#>主动句先摆出 storm，让读者先看造成损坏的来源，再看到 roof 承受动作。<#0.8#>
再看，The roof was damaged by the storm.<#0.7#>被动句把 roof 推到句首；was damaged 说明它受到影响，by 短语才补回风暴。<#0.8#>
最后看，My bike was stolen.<#0.7#>自行车被偷已经是完整重点，偷车的人未知也不重要，没有必要虚加一个施事。<#0.9#>
先问主语是动作发出者还是承受者，再决定主动或被动。施事不知道、不重要或不想强调时，被动句不必硬加 by someone。镜头换了，事件中谁做、谁承受并没有改变。

course.title: Passive chains across tense and aspect
course.meta: Change the finite auxiliary while preserving been/being slots
examples: The road is being repaired now.
The work has been finished already.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: is carries present tense and agrees with room, while cleaned is the past participle; together they form a present-simple passive.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: is carries present tense, being builds the progressive, and passive be selects past-participle repaired; the chain means “currently being repaired.”

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: has carries present tense, been is passive be after perfect have, and finished is the past participle; the chain presents a completed passive result.

rules: A simple passive uses the appropriate tense of be + past participle.
A progressive passive uses be + being + past participle.
A perfect passive uses have + been + past participle.

questions.question: What is the present simple passive pattern?
questions.correct: be carries tense; the participle marks passive voice.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: be carries tense; the participle marks passive voice.

questions.question: How is “currently under repair” formed?
questions.correct: Progressive be doing plus passive be done yields is being repaired.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Progressive be doing plus passive be done yields is being repaired.

questions.question: What is the perfect passive pattern?
questions.correct: been is the participle of passive be after perfect have.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: been is the participle of passive be after perfect have.

narration.text:
被动可以出现在一般、进行和完成等不同时间画面里。看起来动词很多，其实只是在同一条谓语链上叠加“什么时候、怎样展开、谁承受动作”。<#0.9#>
先看，The room is cleaned daily.<#0.7#>is 负责现在和单数一致，cleaned 负责被动；daily 再说明这一动作的规律。<#0.8#>
再看，The road is being repaired now.<#0.7#>道路此刻处在维修过程中，所以进行层和被动层同时出现，形成 is being repaired。<#0.8#>
最后看，The work has been finished already.<#0.7#>工作已经完成，has been finished 把完成结果与被动关系叠在同一条链上。<#0.9#>
从左向右先找限定助动词，再识别进行或完成，最后确认被动结构落在过去分词上。每个形式只承担自己那一层信息。

course.title: The modal predicate system
course.meta: Strength, temporal inference and perfect modals
examples: You must wear a seat belt.
She may have missed the train.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: can is the finite modal expressing ability or possibility; swim stays in the base form, and together they form the complete predicate.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: must adds strong obligation to wear a seat belt; wear is base form, and must wear forms the complete predicate core.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: may marks uncertain inference, while have missed directs it to the earlier event of missing the train; the chain evaluates a past event.

rules: A modal takes no third-person or tense ending and is followed by a base verb.
must, should, may and might express different strengths of obligation, possibility or judgment; context determines the choice.
Modal + have + past participle directs the judgment toward a past event.

questions.question: She can ___ .
questions.correct: A modal takes a base verb.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: A modal takes a base verb.

questions.question: What best expresses strong obligation?
questions.correct: must expresses strong obligation.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: must expresses strong obligation.

questions.question: What does may have missed express?

options.text: Possible inference about a past event

questions.correct: have missed places the modal judgment on a prior event.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: have missed places the modal judgment on a prior event.

narration.text:
情态动词像给动作加一层说话人的态度：能不能、必须不必须、可能不可能。它不替代动作，而是站在动作前面评价这件事。<#0.9#>
先看，She can swim.<#0.7#>can 先给 swim 加上能力意义，而真正动作仍由原形 swim 表达。<#0.8#>
再看，You must wear a seat belt.<#0.7#>must 把“系安全带”变成强义务；wear 不再自己变化。<#0.8#>
最后看，She may have missed the train.<#0.7#>may 表示不确定判断，have missed 把这个判断指向较早发生的误车。<#0.9#>
先确定情态意义，再看它判断的是现在动作还是较早事件。普通情态后接原形；情态加 have done 时，判断被推向过去。选词时还要比较语气强弱，“可能”和“必须”并不是同一种态度。

course.title: Semi-modals and boundary forms
course.meta: have to, be able to and used to mix lexical and auxiliary properties
examples: She has been able to solve it.
Did you use to live here?

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: have to behaves lexically and needs Do for a present question; finiteness is on Do, while have and leave stay in base form.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: has is the finite perfect auxiliary, been is the participle of be, and able to solve is its subject complement; able is not an auxiliary.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: used to expresses a past habit; once Did carries past tense in the question, used returns to base-form use.

rules: have to often expresses external obligation; its questions and negatives normally require do-support.
be able to can occur in more tense and non-finite positions; be carries finiteness.
used to expresses a past habit or state; questions and negatives commonly use did, with used returning to use.

questions.question: Which operator forms a present question with have to?
questions.correct: Modern English normally uses do you have to.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Modern English normally uses do you have to.

questions.question: Which part carries the perfect in has been able to?
questions.correct: have + been forms the perfect chain.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: have + been forms the perfect chain.

questions.question: Which is the standard question structure?
questions.correct: did carries past marking, so use is base form.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: did carries past marking, so use is base form.

narration.text:
have to、able 结构和 used to 意思有点像情态，但语法行为又保留了实义结构的特点，所以不能全部照 can、must 的方法处理。<#0.9#>
先看，Do you have to leave?<#0.7#>have to 自己不能像 must 那样直接前移，这里需要 Do 来承担疑问。<#0.8#>
再看，She has been able to solve it.<#0.7#>完成变化落在 has been 上，able to solve 说明到现在已经具备的能力。<#0.8#>
最后看，Did you use to live here?<#0.7#>Did 已经带走过去标记，后面只能写 use to，不能再让 used 重复过去变化。<#0.9#>
先找真正承担时态和疑问操作的词。半情态的意义可以整体理解，但变否定、疑问或完成时，仍要按它内部的动词结构变化。

course.title: Predicate operations in negatives and questions
course.meta: The operator carries not, inversion and answer repetition

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: Linking is is itself the finite operator, so not follows it directly; ready is the subject complement, and do-support is unnecessary.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: The original arrived has no auxiliary, so Did is inserted and moved forward; past tense shifts to Did and arrive returns to base form.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: Who itself fills the subject slot and called remains the finite past predicate; there is no separate subject to invert with an operator.

rules: Finite be takes not directly and does not use do-support.
A yes-no question moves the operator before the subject; if none exists, do is inserted.
When a wh-word itself is the subject, no subject-operator inversion follows.

questions.question: What is the negative of Mia is ready?
questions.correct: Finite be itself carries negation.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Finite be itself carries negation.

questions.question: Why does the question use arrive?
questions.correct: Operator did carries the clause’s past finiteness.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Operator did carries the clause’s past finiteness.

questions.question: Which asks who called you?
questions.correct: Who is the subject, so do-support is normally absent.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Who is the subject, so do-support is normally absent.

narration.text:
否定和疑问看似要改整句，其实核心动作只有一个：找到限定操作词。它负责接 not，也负责在一般疑问句里移动到主语前。<#0.9#>
先看，Mia is not ready.<#0.7#>is 本身就能接 not，ready 只是表语，因此不用额外增加 do。<#0.8#>
再看，Did they arrive on time?<#0.7#>原句没有助动词，Did 被请到句首承担过去和疑问，arrive 随即恢复原形。<#0.8#>
最后看，Who called you?<#0.7#>Who 就是要寻找的主语，called 直接跟在后面；这里没有另一个主语需要倒装。<#0.9#>
变句前先找 be、助动词或情态词；都没有才用 do 支持。特殊疑问词本身作主语时，不要再多做一次倒装。每次只让一个词承担限定变化，实义动词就不会又变一次。先找开关，再变句。

course.title: Emphatic do
course.meta: Strengthening confirmation, contrast or correction

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: Adding do to the affirmative does not change the event of understanding; it strengthens confirmation or correction.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: does carries emphasis, present tense and third-person agreement, so the lexical verb must be base-form want.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: did carries both emphasis and past tense, so call is not past-marked again; did call means that he really called yesterday.

rules: An affirmative statement can use do/does/did + base form to emphasize truth.
Emphatic do carries tense and agreement; the lexical verb is base form.
To emphasize a past fact, use did + base form, not did + past form.

questions.question: What does do do in I do understand?
questions.correct: do supplies emphasis in an affirmative statement.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: do supplies emphasis in an affirmative statement.

questions.question: Which is correct?
questions.correct: does carries third-person agreement; want is base form.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: does carries third-person agreement; want is base form.

questions.question: How do you say he really called yesterday?
questions.correct: did carries past tense.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: did carries past tense.

narration.text:
肯定句里出现 do、does 或 did，有时不是提问，也不是否定，而是在说“确实如此”。它常用来确认事实、纠正别人或加强对比。<#0.9#>
先看，I do understand you.<#0.7#>do 没有改变 understand 的动作，只把语气加强成“我确实理解”。<#0.8#>
再看，She does want to help.<#0.7#>does 同时扛起强调和三单，want 不能再加 s，否则同一变化会出现两次。<#0.8#>
最后看，He did call yesterday.<#0.7#>过去的强调由 did 负责，所以后面保留 call，而不是再写过去式。<#0.9#>
强调 do 自己承担时态和主谓一致，后面的实义动词必须保持原形。听语气时抓住“确实”，写形式时避免重复变化。句子仍然是肯定陈述，只是说话人把语气特别加重了。

course.title: Short answers and predicate substitution
course.meta: Retain the operator instead of repeating the whole predicate
examples: Has Mia left? Yes, she has.
Mia sings better than Tom does.
Mia can swim, and so can Tom.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: The question’s first auxiliary is Has, so the short answer retains that operator and replaces Mia with she: Yes, she has.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: In the than-clause, does carries present tense and agreement with Tom while substituting for sings to avoid repetition.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: The preceding complete predicate is can swim; so can Tom retains modal operator can and omits repeated swim.

rules: A short answer repeats the operator and agrees with its answer subject.
do/does/did can substitute for a preceding simple-tense lexical predicate.
so/neither + operator + subject can mean “so does...” or “neither does...”; the operator follows the preceding predicate.

questions.question: What is the positive short answer to Has Mia left?
questions.correct: The original operator is has.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The original operator is has.

questions.question: What does does replace?
questions.correct: does replaces repeated predicate sings.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: does replaces repeated predicate sings.

questions.question: Mia can swim, and Tom can too. Which structure fits?
questions.correct: The preceding operator is can.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The preceding operator is can.

narration.text:
英语短答不喜欢把刚说过的整条谓语再念一遍，会留下一个能代表原结构的操作词。比较句和“也一样”结构也使用同样办法。<#0.9#>
先看，Has Mia left? Yes, she has.<#0.7#>问句使用 Has，答语就保留 has；Mia 换成 she 后，不需要再重复 left。<#0.8#>
再看，Mia sings better than Tom does.<#0.7#>does 在比较分句里代替 sings，同时与 Tom 保持现在时和单数一致。<#0.8#>
最后看，Mia can swim, and so can Tom.<#0.7#>前句的关键操作词是 can，所以“Tom 也会”仍保留 can，而不是换成 does。<#0.9#>
先回到前一句找操作词：has 就保留 has，can 就保留 can，一般实义动词则用 do、does 或 did 替代。不要只按中文的“也”来猜。

course.title: Predicate sharing and ellipsis
course.meta: Recover shared auxiliaries or predicates in parallel structures
examples: Mia has finished the report and sent it.
Mia can play the piano, and Tom can, too.
Some reports were accepted, but others were not.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: has scopes over both finished and sent, expandable as has finished... and has sent...; the coordinated lexical verbs share one perfect auxiliary.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: The second clause retains can to preserve the same modal and tense relation; play the piano is omitted because it is fully recoverable.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: others were not retains passive operator were and negator not; accepted is recoverable from the first clause, so passive meaning remains clear.

rules: Coordinated predicates can share one subject and auxiliary.
A shared lexical predicate can be omitted from the second coordinate after an auxiliary and recovered by parallelism.
Ellipsis must leave tense, voice and modality recoverable; retain the full predicate when recovery is unclear.

questions.question: Which auxiliary does sent it share in the perfect construction?
questions.correct: It expands to has finished and has sent.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: It expands to has finished and has sent.

questions.question: What is omitted in Tom can, too?
questions.correct: Operator can remains and stands for the full predicate.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Operator can remains and stands for the full predicate.

questions.question: What is omitted in others were not?
questions.correct: Passive operator were remains; the participle is recovered from the first coordinate.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Passive operator were remains; the participle is recovered from the first coordinate.

narration.text:
并列结构里，相同的信息可以只说一次。看见后半句变短时，不要认为它缺语法成分，而要从前面的平行结构把共享或省略的部分还原出来。<#0.9#>
先看，Mia has finished the report and sent it.<#0.7#>has 同时管 finished 和 sent，两个动作并列共享同一层完成意义。<#0.8#>
再看，Mia can play the piano, and Tom can, too.<#0.7#>Tom 后只留下 can，读者能从前半句恢复 play the piano，所以无需重复。<#0.8#>
最后看，Some reports were accepted, but others were not.<#0.7#>were not 保留被动和否定，省掉的 accepted 能从前一分句唯一找回。<#0.9#>
还原后要检查时态、语态和情态是否仍一致。能唯一恢复才可以省；如果读者可能恢复出不同内容，就应该保留完整谓语。

course.title: Integrated predicate analysis
course.meta: Check finiteness, chain order, tense-aspect, voice, modality and agreement in layers
examples: The road may have been closed.
The work must have been completed.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: may is the sole finite operator, have builds the perfect, and been closed builds the passive; from left to right they form one complete predicate chain.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: must marks the speaker’s judgment, have places the event earlier, and been completed marks passive voice; work receives the action.

exampleNotes.title: Example explained
exampleNotes.body: Check in order: subject → finite operator → auxiliary chain → lexical verb → complements.

rules: In a complex predicate, first find the finite operator, then analyse auxiliary slots to the right.
To interpret a predicate, separately ask when the viewpoint is, how the event unfolds, whether the subject acts or is affected, and what stance is expressed.
Finally check agreement and operations: finite marking appears once, and each following verb form is selected by the preceding auxiliary.

questions.question: What is the finite operator in may have been closed?
questions.correct: The initial modal carries finiteness.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The initial modal carries finiteness.

questions.question: Which systems occur in must have been completed?
questions.correct: must marks stance, have marks perfect, and been completed marks passive.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: must marks stance, have marks perfect, and been completed marks passive.

questions.question: Why is Does the plan seems... incorrect?

options.text: Third-person finiteness is already on Does

questions.correct: The clause cannot mark third-person agreement on both Does and seems.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The clause cannot mark third-person agreement on both Does and seems.

narration.text:
面对长谓语，最稳的方法不是一次翻完，而是像拆积木一样分层：谁承担限定性，后面依次加入了什么时间、语态和情态信息。<#0.9#>
先看，The road may have been closed.<#0.7#>may 是最左边的限定开关，have 加入完成，been closed 再加入被动。<#0.8#>
再看，The work must have been completed.<#0.7#>must 先表达判断，have 把完成放到较早时间，been completed 表明 work 承受动作。<#0.8#>
最后看，Does the plan seem reasonable?<#0.7#>Does 已经承担现在时和三单，seem 必须用原形；reasonable 再说明 plan 的状态。<#0.9#>
综合判断按固定顺序走：主语、限定操作词、助动词链、实义动词、补足成分。每层只标一次，既不会漏，也不会把多个形式误数成多个谓语。
